chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Ja'far from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abu al-'Ala' al-Kaffaf from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) who said:

"Whoever prays the Maghrib prayer, then follows it up without speaking until he prays two rak'ahs, they are recorded for him among the 'Illiyin; and if he prays four, a Hajj Mabrur (accepted pilgrimage) is recorded for him."

key_terms.حَجَّةٌ مَبْرُورَةٌ: An accepted pilgrimage (Hajj) with no sins remaining
key_terms.عَقَّبَ: To follow up (a prayer with voluntary prayers)
key_terms.عِلِّيِّينَ: A high rank in Paradise mentioned in the Quran

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying two or four rak'ahs after Maghrib without speaking?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the virtue of *Mu'aqabah* (voluntary prayers immediately following obligatory ones), emphasizing silence to maintain spiritual presence. The reward of 'Illiyin for two rak'ahs connects to the Quranic description of the righteous, while the 'accepted Hajj' for four rak'ahs underscores the cumulative merit of consistent devotion.
